newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH FINMIN SAYS RIKSBANK DOES NOT DECIDE EMU.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH FINMIN SAYS RIKSBANK DOES NOT DECIDE EMU.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Wednesday the Riksbank's support for early membership of the European single currency would not determine the government's position.
The Riksbank -- central bank -- last week dismissed a report from an official Swedish goverment commission on economic and monetary union that recommended a wait-and-see attitude.
The central bank said Sweden should join EMU from its start on January 1, 1999.
"The Riksbank wants us to join from 1999. I am not convinced about this," Asbrink told reporters after a speech in Linkoping on Wednesday.
"The Riksbank is a heavy authority but there are many others. The Riksbank's view is one part of the foundation on which we will make our decision."
Asbrink, reflecting Swedish fears that EMU will lead to a federal Europe, said he could not predict the political consequences of a single currency with any clarity before much later this year.
"This is a really determining question but I am not certain that we will have any answer by the autumn," Asbrink said.
"That I, (Prime Minister) Goran Persson, and many others are against a development that means control from the top is no secret. This scepticism exists in many other countries also."
